paragraphs: Miovision sells traffic data collection tools meant to give planners the accurate, verifiable data their mobility plans depend on. It also sells detection equipment that improves signal performance by responding to real-world road user demand, from bicycles to articulated trucks. Its Opticom line clears the path for emergency fleets without re-timing entire corridors.

Portable devices capture comprehensive multimodal count data including cars, trucks, pedestrians and bikes. A newer optimization product replaces manual five-year retiming cycles with iterative, objective-based optimization that the company says cuts manual effort by up to half. Engineers compare plans side-by-side, validate against industry standards, and push updates directly to field controllers without manual data re-entry.

The company says that since 2005 it has had 2,000 customers in 68 countries and 13,000 cities, with 30 billion vehicles and 1.5 billion pedestrians counted. It lists more than 300 detection customers in North America. Detroit partnered with Miovision to upgrade over 600 intersections. In San Rafael, police and fire vehicles now receive signal priority at 53 intersections.

quote.text: Clear the path for your emergency fleets without re-timing entire corridors.
